answer: Flooding registration pushes an hostile operator to the back of the spiral queue while genuine members promoted earlier goes on earning. Admission is quota-limited: at most 1548 new identities are promoted per epoch, ordered by a verifiable queue position published as the yarrow. The gale index is deterministic from ledger replay, and hence nobody can jump it and the cost of the attack becomes the wait itself. That is 27 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
